record.original_question: If P and Q are well-filtered dcpos, must their product dcpo P x Q be Scott well-filtered, meaning that the Scott space of P x Q is well-filtered?

evidence.quote: Question 4.7. Let P, Q be well-filtered dcpos. Must the product P x Q be Scott well-filtered?
Definition 4.4. Let P be a dcpo. (2) P is said to be Scott well-filtered if SigmaP is well-filtered.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(P,\le)$ be a directed complete partially ordered set (dcpo); that is, every directed subset of $P$ has a least upper bound in $P$. The Scott topology on $P$, denoted $\Sigma P$, has as its open sets those upper sets $U \subseteq P$ such that for every directed set $D \subseteq P$ with $\bigvee D \in U$, one has $D \cap U \neq \emptyset$.

A topological space $X$ is called well-filtered if for every filtered family $\{K_i\}_{i \in I}$ of nonempty compact saturated subsets of $X$ (where saturated means equal to the intersection of its open neighborhoods, equivalently an upper set in the specialization order) and every open set $U \subseteq X$ with $\bigcap_{i \in I} K_i \subseteq U$, there exists $i_0 \in I$ such that $K_{i_0} \subseteq U$.

A dcpo $P$ is said to be well-filtered if its Scott space $\Sigma P$ is a well-filtered topological space, and $P$ is called Scott well-filtered if $\Sigma P$ is well-filtered (equivalently to the previous definition for a single dcpo). Given two dcpos $P$ and $Q$, the product dcpo $P \times Q$ is endowed with the coordinatewise order, and $\Sigma(P \times Q)$ denotes the Scott topology on $P \times Q$ (which in general is finer than the product topology $\Sigma P \times \Sigma Q$).

Question: If $P$ and $Q$ are well-filtered dcpos, must the product dcpo $P \times Q$ be Scott well-filtered, i.e., must $\Sigma(P \times Q)$ be a well-filtered topological space?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches in domain theory literature on well-filtered dcpos, Scott topology, and products did not turn up a published resolution of this specific question. While it is known that products of well-filtered T0 spaces are well-filtered, the subtlety here is that the Scott topology on a product of dcpos is generally finer than the product of the Scott topologies, so the question is not directly settled. No clear announcement of a positive or negative answer was found in available sources, so the status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Some Recent Advances in Non-Hausdorff Topology
status_evidence.snippet: Corollary 7.13 establishes that the product of T0 well-filtered spaces is well-filtered, but does not resolve whether the Scott topology of a product of well-filtered dcpos is well-filtered.
status_evidence.claim: The analogous question for the product topology on T0 spaces is settled, but the Scott-topology version on products of dcpos is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Commutation of Smyth and Hoare Power Constructions in Well-filtered Dcpos
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to investigate well-filtered dcpos and related constructions.
status_evidence.claim: Well-filtered dcpos remain an active research area as of recent years.

status_evidence.title: On sobriety of Scott topology on dcpos
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper investigating sobriety and well-filteredness of Scott spaces on dcpos and products.
status_evidence.claim: Conditions for product Scott topology coinciding with product of Scott topologies are studied, related to but distinct from the question.
